title: Buddhist Philosophy: The Middle Way to the End of Suffering

questions.question: The Second Noble Truth identifies the cause of suffering as:
questions.rationale: The Four Noble Truths run: dukkha (suffering), samudaya (its arising from craving, tanha), nirodha (its cessation), and magga (the Eightfold Path).

questions.question: The eight factors of the path are grouped into three trainings. Which set is correct?
questions.rationale: Wisdom (right view, right intention), ethical conduct (right speech, action, livelihood), and mental discipline (right effort, mindfulness, concentration).

questions.question: The doctrine of anatta claims that:
options: The atman is identical with Brahman
There is no permanent self — only a stream of changing aggregates
The self is created by God
questions.rationale: Anatta (no-self) denies a permanent atman: what exists is a stream of five skandhas — form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness.

questions.question: Pratityasamutpada — dependent origination — is best summarised as:
options: All things arise from a creator
All things arise permanently and unchangingly
This being, that becomes; with the ceasing of this, that ceases
questions.rationale: The twelve-link nidana chain expresses the causal law: each link arises dependent on the previous one, so ending one ends the rest — which is how suffering can be ended.

questions.question: How does Buddhism explain rebirth without a soul?
options: The atman travels to a new body
The same person is reborn unchanged
Like a flame lighting a new candle — causally continuous, neither the same nor different
Rebirth is an illusion of the gods
questions.rationale: The candle-flame analogy: karmic continuity without a permanent self, just as the second flame depends on the first without being identical to it.

questions.question: Which vehicle upholds the bodhisattva ideal of universal liberation?
questions.rationale: Mahayana (Sanskritic, East Asian) makes the bodhisattva its ideal; Theravada (Pali, 'the elders') emphasises the arhat's personal liberation.

questions.question: Nagarjuna's concept of shunyata (emptiness) means:
options: The world is made of empty space
The mind is a blank tablet
questions.rationale: Since everything arises dependently on conditions, nothing has independent essence — emptiness is the absence of own-being, not literal non-existence.

questions.question: The Yogacara school, founded by Asanga and Vasubandhu, taught:
options: Representation-only (vijnapti-matra) — we know only mental content
questions.rationale: Yogacara holds that the external world is a construction of consciousness, including a storehouse consciousness (alaya-vijnana).

questions.question: The Third Buddhist Council, held around 250 BCE at Pataliputra, was patronised by:
questions.rationale: The councils ran: Rajagriha (Ajatashatru), Vaishali c. 383 BCE (Kalasoka), Pataliputra c. 250 BCE (Ashoka), Kashmir 1st century CE (Kanishka).

questions.question: Dignaga and Dharmakirti accepted which two pramanas?
questions.rationale: Buddhist epistemology accepted only perception and inference, and analysed meaning through apoha — words work by excluding what a thing is not.
